claim: The default cooldown of an Auto Scaling group is 300 seconds (5 minutes).
question: What is the default cooldown period of an Auto Scaling group?

evidence.quote: By default, this cooldown period is set to 300 seconds (5 minutes).
If the default cooldown is not defined, the default value of 300 seconds is used.

claim: In the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling console, you cannot set the default cooldown when you first create a group; you can update it after the group exists.
question: Can you set the default cooldown when you create an Auto Scaling group in the console?

evidence.quote: You can't set the default cooldown when you initially create an Auto Scaling group in the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling console.
If needed, you can update this after the group is created.

claim: After a group launches or terminates instances, further scaling activities started by simple scaling policies wait for the cooldown period to end.
question: Which scaling policy type waits for the cooldown period?

values.display: scaling activities initiated by simple scaling policies
values.spoken: scaling activities started by simple scaling policies

evidence.quote: After your Auto Scaling group launches or terminates instances, it waits for a cooldown period to end before any further scaling activities initiated by simple scaling policies can start.

claim: Target tracking and step scaling policies can start a scale-out immediately without waiting for the cooldown period to end; new instances have a warmup period instead.
question: Do target tracking and step scaling policies wait for the cooldown period?

values.display: without waiting for the cooldown period to end
values.spoken: without waiting for the cooldown to end

evidence.quote: Target tracking and step scaling policies can initiate a scale-out activity immediately without waiting for the cooldown period to end.
Instead, whenever your Auto Scaling group launches instances, the individual instances have a warmup period.

claim: A scheduled action can start a scaling activity at its scheduled time without waiting for the cooldown period to end.
question: Does a scheduled action wait for the cooldown period?

evidence.quote: When a scheduled action starts at the scheduled time, it can also initiate a scaling activity immediately without waiting for the cooldown period to end.

claim: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling does not wait for the cooldown period to end before it replaces an unhealthy instance.
question: Does the cooldown period delay the replacement of an unhealthy instance?

values.display: does not wait for the cooldown period
values.spoken: does not wait for the cooldown period

evidence.quote: If an instance becomes unhealthy, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling does not wait for the cooldown period to end before replacing the unhealthy instance.

claim: Manual scaling does not wait for a cooldown by default; with the AWS CLI or an SDK you can choose to honor the default cooldown.
question: Does manual scaling wait for the cooldown period by default?

values.display: the default is not to wait
values.spoken: the default is not to wait

evidence.quote: When you manually scale your Auto Scaling group, the default is not to wait for a cooldown to end.
However, you can override this behavior and honor the default cooldown when you use the AWS CLI or an SDK to manually scale.

claim: When several instances launch or terminate, the cooldown period starts when the last instance finishes launching or terminating.
question: When does the cooldown period start when several instances launch at once?

values.display: when the last instance finishes launching or terminating
values.spoken: when the last instance finishes launching or terminating

evidence.quote: When multiple instances launch or terminate, the cooldown period (either the default cooldown or the scaling policy-specific cooldown) takes effect starting when the last instance finishes launching or terminating.

claim: Simple scaling policies use the group's default cooldown unless a cooldown is set on the policy, which then overrides the default cooldown.
question: Can a simple scaling policy have its own cooldown?

evidence.quote: By default, all simple scaling policies use the default cooldown period that is defined for the Auto Scaling group.
When a cooldown period is specified for a policy, it overrides the default cooldown.

claim: By default, Elastic Load Balancing waits 300 seconds to complete deregistration (connection draining).
question: How long does Elastic Load Balancing wait for connection draining by default?

evidence.quote: By default, Elastic Load Balancing waits 300 seconds to complete the deregistration (connection draining) process.

claim: With Elastic Load Balancing, for scale in, the cooldown period starts when the instance selected for termination starts connection draining; it does not wait for draining or a lifecycle hook to finish.
question: When does the cooldown start on scale in when the group uses Elastic Load Balancing?

evidence.quote: When Elastic Load Balancing is enabled, for the purposes of scaling in, the cooldown period starts when the instance that's selected for termination starts connection draining (deregistration delay).
The cooldown period doesn't wait for connection draining to finish or the lifecycle hook to complete its action.

note: The Considerations list of the same page also says: 'If the group is behind an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer, it will wait for the terminating instances to deregister before starting the cooldown period.' The two statements of the page disagree; writers should not test the exact start point.

claim: AWS recommends as a best practice not to use simple scaling policies and scaling cooldowns; target tracking or step scaling performs better.
question: Does AWS recommend simple scaling policies with cooldowns?

values.display: do not use simple scaling policies
values.spoken: do not use simple scaling policies

evidence.quote: As a best practice, we recommend that you do not use simple scaling policies and scaling cooldowns.
A target tracking scaling policy or a step scaling policy is better for scaling performance.

claim: The default instance warmup is not enabled or configured by default; AWS strongly recommends enabling it for target tracking and step scaling.
question: Is the default instance warmup turned on by default?

values.display: not enabled or configured by default
values.spoken: not enabled or configured by default

evidence.quote: To optimize the performance of your target tracking and step scaling policies, we strongly recommend that you enable and configure the default instance warmup. It is not enabled or configured by default.

claim: Without a default instance warmup, instance refresh uses the health check grace period, target tracking and step scaling policies use the default cooldown, and predictive scaling policies have no default warmup time.
question: Which warmup does each feature use when no default instance warmup is set?

values.display: value set for the default cooldown
values.spoken: value set for the default cooldown

qualifiers.condition: no default instance warmup is set

evidence.quote: For example, if you don't set a default instance warmup, the instance refresh feature uses the health check grace period as the default warmup time. If you have any target tracking and step scaling policies, they use the value set for the default cooldown as the default warmup time. If you have any predictive scaling policies, they have no default warmup time.

claim: If you are unsure of the warmup time, AWS suggests starting with 300 seconds and then adjusting it.
question: What warmup value does AWS suggest as a starting point?

evidence.quote: If you're not sure how much time you need for the warmup time, you could start with 300 seconds.

claim: While new instances warm up, dynamic scaling blocks scale-in activities until they finish warming up.
question: Can dynamic scaling scale in while new instances are still warming up?

values.display: blocks the scale in activities for dynamic scaling

evidence.quote: If demand decreases, dynamic scaling becomes more conservative to protect your application's availability. This blocks the scale in activities for dynamic scaling until the new instances finish warming up.

claim: Until its warmup time has expired, a new instance is not counted toward the group's aggregated EC2 instance metrics.
question: What does the instance warmup change for scaling metrics?

values.display: not counted toward the aggregated EC2 instance metrics
values.spoken: not counted in the aggregated metrics

evidence.quote: Until its specified warmup time has expired, an instance is not counted toward the aggregated EC2 instance metrics of the Auto Scaling group.

claim: The default health check grace period is 300 seconds when you create a group in the console, and 0 seconds when you create it with the AWS CLI or an SDK.
question: What is the default health check grace period?

qualifiers.condition: 300 seconds in the console; 0 seconds with the AWS CLI or an SDK

evidence.quote: In the console, by default, the health check grace period is 300 seconds when you create an Auto Scaling group. Its default value is 0 seconds when you create an Auto Scaling group using the AWS CLI or an SDK.

claim: A health check grace period of 0 turns the grace period off.
question: What does a health check grace period of 0 mean?

values.spoken: a value of zero turns it off

evidence.quote: A value of 0 turns off the health check grace period.

claim: If you use lifecycle hooks for instance launch, you can set the health check grace period to 0, and a value set too high reduces the effectiveness of health checks.
question: What grace period fits a group that uses launch lifecycle hooks?

values.display: set the health check grace period to 0
values.spoken: set the grace period to zero

evidence.quote: Setting this value too high reduces the effectiveness of the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling health checks.
If you use lifecycle hooks for instance launch, you can set the health check grace period to 0.

claim: The health check grace period is the minimum time, in seconds, that a new instance stays in service before Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling terminates it for being unhealthy.
question: What does the health check grace period control?

values.spoken: minimum amount of time in seconds

evidence.quote: The health check grace period specifies the minimum amount of time (in seconds) to keep a new instance in service before terminating it if it's found to be unhealthy.
